title: no test exercises BudgetExceeded propagation through build_first_valid_path
description: tests/build_first_valid_path.rs covers: positive (tc60), NoValidPath (AlwaysRejectVerifier), NoPathFound (empty pool). It does NOT cover BudgetExceeded propagation, despite the rustdoc explicitly documenting that variant (lib.rs:934-935: "DepthExceeded / BudgetExceeded — propagated from build_path_candidates when the iterator surfaces them"). Risk: a future refactor of the propagation path (e.g., a well-intentioned contributor folding BudgetExceeded into NoValidPath because "they're both no-path results") will silently change semantics with no test failure. The fixture pattern from tests/integration.rs:test_iterator_budget_bounded_across_calls is reusable — a budget-tight config on a pool that yields one rejected candidate before exhaustion would exercise the propagation. Also missing: DepthExceeded propagation, but that's less critical because the depth-probe logic in build_first_valid_path_with_config (lib.rs:1031-1042) has its own subtle case-split between "zero candidates yielded → probe" and "some candidates yielded but all rejected → NoValidPath wins".
close_reason:
Fixed -- test added: an_exhausted_budget_propagates_verbatim_and_is_not_reported_as_no_valid_path in pkix-path-builder/tests/build_first_valid_path.rs.

The bead was accurate. Checked all three candidate homes first: integration.rs exercises BudgetExceeded through build_path (not this entry point); review_adversarial_pool.rs asserts the OPPOSITE property (40 decoys must not exhaust the budget when a valid depth-1 path exists, so it panics on BudgetExceeded); and the dedicated build_first_valid_path.rs file never mentioned the budget at all.

What the test pins is the contract behind Some(Err(e)) => return Err(e): BudgetExceeded must come back verbatim, not folded into NoValidPath. NoValidPath claims every candidate was built and rejected, whereas an exhausted budget means most were never constructed -- the search is inconclusive and a path may exist past the cut-off. A caller retrying with a larger budget, or reporting "could not decide" rather than "untrusted", needs those apart.

Driven through build_first_valid_path_with_config with dfs_budget = 1 (one unit buys one DFS frame or one candidate examined). A control call at the default budget validates the same PKITS 4.1.1 chain first, so the test cannot pass on a pool that was never solvable.

Verified by mutation rather than by it passing: wrapping the propagation in NoValidPath makes it fail with "expected BudgetExceeded to propagate verbatim, got NoValidPath { tried: 0, last_error: ... }". Note there are three identical propagation lines in lib.rs (1013 in build_path_with_config, 1163 and 1196 in build_first_valid_path_with_config); 1163 is the one this test drives.

Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, 2340 tests.
